rules.statement: Make a handler for cross-replica broadcast or invalidation messages idempotent, so a message that is lost, repeated, late, or out of order leaves the state correct.
rules.why: Delivery is best effort, at most once, and unordered, and the publisher's own replica also receives its message, so a handler may run twice for one change.
rules.check: Look for broadcast or pub/sub handlers that assume one delivery, assume ordering, or do non-idempotent work such as incrementing, appending, or one-time side effects.

rules.statement: When a broadcaster dispatches a message to several handlers, catch and log each handler's failure, keep delivering to the other handlers, and never pass the failure back to the publisher.
rules.why: One faulty handler must not stop other features from getting the hint or fail the operation that published it.
rules.check: Look for dispatch loops over handlers that have no per-handler try/catch, that stop at the first exception, or that rethrow to the caller of PublishAsync.

rules.statement: Treat a cache-invalidation announcement as a hint only: every cache it invalidates still needs a bounded absolute lifetime or a polling fallback, so a replica that missed the message converges anyway.
rules.why: Announcements can be lost, for example when a publisher can't reach the broker. A sliding expiration alone keeps a busy entry stale forever.
rules.check: Look for caches that rely only on broadcast invalidation, or that use only a sliding expiration with no absolute lifetime or periodic refresh.

rules.statement: When a pub/sub subscription is first established or restored after a reconnect, have the handlers assume they missed messages and invalidate everything they cached.
rules.why: Messages published before the subscription took effect, or while the connection was down, never reached the replica.
rules.check: Look for subscribers that don't call a missed-message or invalidate-all path after subscribing or on a connection-restored event.

rules.statement: Publish a change notification only after the write has committed, put the publish in a finally block so a failed follow-up step still announces it, and log and swallow a publish failure instead of failing the write.
rules.why: The change is committed either way. A notification outage must not fail a management write, and other replicas converge through the bounded fallback.
rules.check: Look for notifications sent before the commit, publishes skipped when a later step throws, or publish exceptions that reach the caller of a committed write.

rules.statement: Hand each incoming pub/sub message to its handlers on a thread-pool thread, not inline on the connection's receive loop.
rules.why: A slow handler must never block the connection from receiving other messages.
rules.check: Look for subscription callbacks that await or run handler work synchronously inside the message-receive callback.

rules.statement: Register a default adapter for an extensibility port with TryAdd so that a host's earlier registration wins, and register handlers that can coexist with TryAddEnumerable.
rules.why: A host that registered its own implementation first must keep it, and several handlers may share one channel.
rules.check: Look for AddSingleton/AddScoped of default port implementations where TryAdd is needed, or multi-handler registrations that use Add or TryAdd instead of TryAddEnumerable.

rules.statement: Prefix pub/sub channel names on a shared broker with the configured key prefix, the same way keys are prefixed.
rules.why: The prefix keeps separate deployments that share one server from receiving each other's messages.
rules.check: Look for PUBLISH or SUBSCRIBE calls that use a raw channel name without the configured key prefix.

rules.why: Channels are an open vocabulary of names compared ordinally, so matching must not depend on culture.
rules.check: Look for channel-name matching that uses culture-sensitive or case-insensitive comparison, or default comparers, instead of StringComparer.Ordinal.
